answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks via correlated-fault joint slashing: agents form stake pools; an atlas maps pool edges in the graph, a sable edge flags bad actors. If anyone in a pool is caught sybiling, the whole pool's stake burns. Honest agents join only trusted-edge pools, segregating from risky clusters. A 500-clone attacker needs 500 distinct trusted pools, each needing real trust across separate chains, capped by honest pool capacity not id count. Attackers cannot pool stake across clones: one bad apple sinks the whole pool, basalt burns.
